title: Internal Hom from the countable free module is a product
statement: Let J be a small site, R a commutative ring sheaf, and N an R-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use the underlying ring convention of [def-weil-pbc-local-coefficient-localization]. Let P be the coproduct of unit modules indexed by lifted natural numbers. The internal Hom sheaf from P to N [def-pur-sheaf-hom], together with the natural-number-indexed maps obtained by precomposing with a basis inclusion and evaluating at 1, is a product of the copies of N. No finiteness of rank, flatness of N, or exactness of products is assumed.

proof.text: Use the existing SheafOfModules.tensorHomAdjunction and its naturality in the first tensor variable to construct a parametrized adjunction. Tensoring on the left is a left adjoint; braiding identifies tensoring on the right with it. Hence these tensor functors preserve coproducts. Mathlib ParametrizedAdjunction.preservesLimitsOfShape_flip_obj implies that internal Hom in its source preserves the opposite free coproduct cone.

proof.text: Evaluation at 1, SheafOfModules.homObjUnitIso, identifies each factor with N. Transport the product property through these isomorphisms: lift a cone after composing all projections with the inverse unit isomorphism, and use the original limit fac and hom_ext to check the result. The resulting projections are exactly precomposition with the basis inclusion followed by evaluation.

theorem countableFree_internalHom_product
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u})
    (N : ringedSiteModules.{u} (localCoefficientRings R)) :
    Nonempty (IsLimit (Fan.mk (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := R)
      (SheafOfModules.free (ULift.{u} ℕ)) N)
      (fun n : ℕ ↦ SheafOfModules.homObjMap.{u, u, u, u} (R := R)
        (SheafOfModules.ιFree (R := localCoefficientRings R) (ULift.up.{u} n)) (𝟙 N) ≫
        (SheafOfModules.homObjUnitIso (R := R) N).hom)))
